Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin — General Coverage Criteria
Policy Number: AET-CPB-2024-15
Effective Date: April 1, 2024

COVERAGE DETERMINATION STANDARD
Aetna considers a service medically necessary when it is required to
identify or treat a member's illness or injury and meets accepted
standards of medicine. Services that are primarily for the convenience
of the member or provider, or that are duplicative of a previously
performed and paid service, are not covered.

DUPLICATE CLAIM POLICY
A claim is considered a duplicate when the same procedure code, same
date of service, same rendering provider, and same patient appear on a
previously adjudicated claim. Duplicate claims are denied under reason
code CO-18 unless the second claim includes modifier -76 (repeat
procedure by same physician) or modifier -77 (repeat procedure by
another physician) with supporting clinical documentation explaining
the medical necessity of the repeat service.

REQUIRED CLAIM ELEMENTS
Every submitted claim must contain complete patient eligibility
information, an accurate ICD-10 diagnosis code that is an exact match
to the documented condition in the medical record, an appropriate CPT
or HCPCS code, the correct place-of-service code, and rendering
provider NPI. Claims with mismatched or unsupported diagnosis-to-
procedure code combinations are subject to automated coding edits and
may be denied under reason code CO-11 (diagnosis inconsistent with
procedure).

BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES
Outpatient behavioral health visits do not require precertification for
the first 8 visits per calendar year. Visits beyond this threshold
require submission of a treatment plan and precertification approval.

Aetna Commercial and Medicare Advantage — Precertification Policy
Policy Number: AET-PC-2024-03
Effective Date: February 1, 2024

PRECERTIFICATION REQUIREMENTS
Aetna requires precertification (prior authorization) for the following
services across all commercial and Medicare Advantage plans:
1. All non-emergent inpatient admissions.
2. Advanced imaging procedures including MRI, CT, and nuclear cardiology
   studies performed in an outpatient setting.
3. Elective surgical procedures with a global surgery period of 90 days
   or more.
4. Home health services beyond the first 60 days following an inpatient
   discharge.
5. Genetic and molecular diagnostic testing panels.

REQUIRED SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION
Requests must include a completed precertification request form, the
ordering physician's clinical notes, relevant lab or imaging results,
and the specific ICD-10 and CPT codes for the requested service. Aetna
will not process a precertification request that lacks a signed
physician order.

CLAIMS SUBMITTED WITHOUT PRECERTIFICATION
Claims for services requiring precertification that are submitted
without an approved precertification number will be denied under
reason code CO-197. Providers have 60 calendar days from the date of
denial to submit a retrospective review request with clinical
justification for why precertification was not obtained in advance.

MODIFIER REQUIREMENTS
Claims billed with modifier -25 (significant, separately identifiable
E/M service) or modifier -59 (distinct procedural service) must include
supporting documentation in the medical record clearly justifying the
use of the modifier. Claims with these modifiers lacking supporting
documentation are subject to automatic review and possible denial.

APPEALS PROCESS
Members and providers may appeal a precertification-related denial
within 180 days. Appeals should be submitted in writing and include all
clinical documentation that supports medical necessity, along with a
detailed explanation addressing the specific denial reason cited.

Blue Cross Blue Shield — Coverage and Claims Adjudication Guidelines
Policy Number: BCBS-CA-2024-18
Effective Date: June 1, 2024

COVERAGE STANDARD
BCBS covers services that are medically necessary and consistent with
nationally recognized clinical guidelines. Coverage determinations are
based on the clinical documentation submitted with, or available to
support, the claim.

CLAIM COMPLETENESS REQUIREMENTS
A complete claim includes: patient and subscriber identification
information, rendering and billing provider NPI, date(s) of service,
place of service code, ICD-10 diagnosis code(s), CPT/HCPCS procedure
code(s), units of service, and billed charges. Claims missing any
required field are rejected prior to adjudication and are not counted
against timely filing limits if resubmitted within 30 days of
rejection.

DUPLICATE CLAIM HANDLING
BCBS's claims editing system flags any claim matching an existing paid
or pending claim on patient, date of service, procedure code, and
rendering provider as a potential duplicate. Duplicate claims are
denied under reason code CO-18 unless accompanied by an appropriate
modifier (-76, -77, -91) and documentation supporting a distinct,
medically necessary repeat service.

MODIFIER AND BUNDLING EDITS
Claims are subject to National Correct Coding Initiative (NCCI) edits.
Procedure code combinations that are bundled under NCCI and billed
without an appropriate modifier will have the component code denied as
included in the primary procedure.

Blue Cross Blue Shield — Prior Authorization Requirements
Policy Number: BCBS-PA-2024-05
Effective Date: February 15, 2024

SERVICES REQUIRING PRIOR AUTHORIZATION
Blue Cross Blue Shield (BCBS) requires prior authorization for:
1. Inpatient hospital admissions (non-emergent).
2. Advanced imaging services (MRI, CT, PET, nuclear medicine studies).
3. Outpatient surgical procedures performed in an ambulatory surgery
   center with an allowed amount exceeding $2,000.
4. Home infusion therapy and specialty pharmaceuticals.
5. Applied behavior analysis (ABA) therapy beyond the initial evaluation.

DOCUMENTATION REQUIRED
Requests must include a completed prior authorization form, clinical
notes from the ordering or treating physician, relevant diagnostic
results, and accurate ICD-10 and CPT/HCPCS codes. BCBS reviews requests
within 5 business days for standard requests and 72 hours for expedited
(urgent) requests.

DENIALS FOR MISSING AUTHORIZATION
Claims for services requiring prior authorization that are submitted
without an approval on file are denied under reason code CO-197.
Network providers may not bill the member for the denied amount
(no balance billing) except in cases where the member was notified in
advance in writing and agreed to be financially responsible.

APPEAL RIGHTS
Providers may file a first-level appeal within 180 days of the denial
notice. The appeal must include all supporting clinical documentation
and a written statement addressing the specific basis for the original
denial.

Cigna Healthcare — Medical Necessity and Coverage Guidelines
Policy Number: CIG-MN-2024-22
Effective Date: May 1, 2024

MEDICAL NECESSITY DEFINITION
Cigna defines a medically necessary service as one that is required to
diagnose or treat an illness, injury, disease, or its symptoms, is in
accordance with generally accepted standards of medical practice, and
is not solely for the convenience of the patient or provider.

CODING ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS
Claims must reflect the most specific ICD-10 code supported by clinical
documentation. Unspecified diagnosis codes (e.g., codes ending in
'.9' where a more specific code exists) may trigger additional review
and are a common cause of claim delay. CPT codes must accurately reflect
the complexity and content of the service rendered; upcoding or
downcoding relative to the documented note is grounds for claim denial
and potential audit.

MISSING PHYSICIAN NOTES
Cigna requires that a signed physician note or operative report be
available to support every billed service. Claims for which supporting
documentation cannot be produced upon request are subject to denial and
potential recoupment of previously paid amounts under reason code
CO-B7.

TIMELY FILING
Claims must be submitted within 120 days of the date of service.
Claims submitted after this window will be denied under reason code
CO-29 (timely filing limit expired) regardless of medical necessity.

Cigna Healthcare — Prior Authorization and Utilization Management Policy
Policy Number: CIG-UM-2024-09
Effective Date: January 15, 2024

SERVICES REQUIRING PRIOR AUTHORIZATION
Cigna requires prior authorization for:
1. All elective inpatient admissions and skilled nursing facility
   admissions.
2. Outpatient advanced imaging (MRI, CT, PET).
3. Spinal surgery, joint replacement surgery, and bariatric surgery.
4. Specialty infusion drugs administered outside the home setting.
5. Durable medical equipment rentals or purchases exceeding $750.

DOCUMENTATION STANDARDS
All prior authorization requests must include the treating physician's
clinical rationale, relevant diagnostic imaging or lab results, a
description of conservative treatments already attempted (where
applicable), and the specific ICD-10 and CPT/HCPCS codes for the
requested service. Incomplete requests will be returned to the
requesting provider without a determination.

CLAIMS WITHOUT PRIOR AUTHORIZATION
Services rendered without required prior authorization will be denied
under reason code CO-197. Cigna does not guarantee retrospective
authorization; requests for retrospective review must be submitted
within 90 days of the date of service and must include a clear
explanation of any extenuating circumstances (e.g., emergent
conversion from an outpatient to inpatient procedure).

PRIOR AUTHORIZATION VALIDITY
An approved prior authorization is valid for 90 days from the date of
approval unless otherwise specified on the authorization letter. Claims
submitted after the authorization has expired will be treated as if no
authorization was obtained.

APPEALS
Cigna allows two levels of internal appeal. Level 1 appeals must be
submitted within 180 days of the denial and are reviewed by a clinician
who was not involved in the original determination. Level 2 appeals
require new clinical information not previously considered.

UnitedHealthcare Commercial Plan — Coverage Determination Guidelines
Policy Number: UHC-CD-2024-07
Effective Date: March 1, 2024

GENERAL COVERAGE PRINCIPLES
UnitedHealthcare covers services that are medically necessary, consistent
with generally accepted standards of medical practice, and not primarily
for the convenience of the patient or provider.

MEDICAL NECESSITY CRITERIA
A service is considered medically necessary when documentation
establishes all of the following:
1. The service is appropriate for the symptoms, diagnosis, or treatment
   of the member's condition, illness, or injury.
2. The service is provided for the diagnosis or direct treatment of the
   condition, not for screening purposes unless explicitly listed as a
   covered preventive benefit.
3. The service is delivered in accordance with generally accepted
   standards of medical practice.
4. The service is not primarily for the convenience of the patient,
   physician, or other health care provider.
5. Clinical documentation supports the level of service billed.

EXCLUDED SERVICES
The following are generally excluded from coverage unless a specific
plan rider states otherwise:
- Cosmetic procedures not related to reconstructive necessity following
  injury or disease
- Experimental or investigational treatments not approved by the FDA for
  the specific diagnosis billed
- Services rendered without a valid physician order
- Duplicate services billed for the same date of service and same
  provider without documented medical justification

DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS FOR CLAIM SUBMISSION
Every claim must include: patient demographic and eligibility
information, ICD-10 diagnosis code(s) that support medical necessity,
CPT/HCPCS procedure code(s) consistent with the documented service,
rendering provider NPI, and the date of service. Claims missing any of
the above elements will be returned or denied as incomplete
(reason code CO-16).

UnitedHealthcare Commercial Plan — Prior Authorization Policy
Policy Number: UHC-PA-2024-11
Effective Date: January 1, 2024

SCOPE
This policy applies to all UnitedHealthcare Commercial PPO and HMO plans
for outpatient and inpatient procedures billed under CPT codes in the
surgical, advanced imaging, and durable medical equipment categories.

PRIOR AUTHORIZATION REQUIRED SERVICES
The following categories of service require prior authorization before
the service is rendered. Claims submitted without an approved
authorization number on file will be denied.

1. Advanced imaging: MRI, MRA, CT, and PET scans (CPT 70000–79999 range)
   require prior authorization except when performed in an emergency
   department setting with a documented emergency diagnosis.
2. Inpatient surgical procedures with an expected length of stay greater
   than 23 hours require prior authorization at least 3 business days
   before the scheduled procedure date.
3. Durable medical equipment (DME) with a purchase or rental cost
   exceeding $500 requires prior authorization.
4. Physical therapy, occupational therapy, and chiropractic services
   beyond the initial 12 visits per calendar year require prior
   authorization to continue coverage.
5. Specialty pharmacy and infusion therapy administered in an outpatient

authorization to continue coverage.
5. Specialty pharmacy and infusion therapy administered in an outpatient
   facility require prior authorization regardless of cost.

REQUIRED DOCUMENTATION FOR PRIOR AUTHORIZATION SUBMISSION
- Physician order signed and dated by the ordering provider
- Clinical notes supporting medical necessity, including relevant
  diagnostic test results
- ICD-10 diagnosis code(s) supporting the medical necessity of the
  requested service
- CPT/HCPCS code(s) for the requested procedure or equipment
- For DME: a Letter of Medical Necessity (LMN)

CLAIM DENIAL FOR MISSING PRIOR AUTHORIZATION
Claims for services listed above submitted without a valid prior
authorization reference number will be denied with reason code
CO-197 (Precertification/Authorization Absent). Providers may submit a
retroactive authorization request within 180 days of the date of
service, accompanied by a written explanation of the extenuating
circumstances, but retroactive approval is not guaranteed.

APPEALS
A denial issued for lack of prior authorization may be appealed within
180 days of the denial notice. The appeal must include the missing
authorization documentation and a cover letter explaining why prior
authorization could not be obtained before the service was rendered.
